input.step_by_step_reasoning:
1) Nodes: I transcribed the 9 entities drawn on the whiteboard. Each one matches an exact service name in the vocabulary: S3, StepFunctions, MediaConvert, Rekognition, Transcribe, Comprehend, DynamoDB, EC2 and EKS. EC2 and EKS are two different services. Together they form the green 'Reach Engine' box, so I kept them as separate nodes and recorded the Reach Engine role in both notes. The speaker says the step function 'triggers some lambdas' to pull out checksums and technical metadata. No Lambda is drawn, and the ledger shows the arrow going MediaConvert -> DynamoDB. Adding Lambda would mean re-routing a ledger edge, which the rules forbid, so I put this detail in the notes instead. The uploading user is a generic human actor and is not in the entity list, so I removed it. S3 is the entry point.
2) Ledger: there are 9 visual_connections entries, and I emitted one edge for each with the same direction.
3) Extra edge from the audio: the speaker says 'we're going to trigger an ingest into Reach Engine', and Reach Engine runs on both EC2 and EKS. Without a connection, EKS would be an orphan node, so I added DynamoDB -> EKS as a parallel step to DynamoDB -> EC2.
4) Flows: flow 0 is the upload trigger plus the MediaConvert proxy and technical metadata. Flow 1 is Rekognition video analysis. Flow 2 is Transcribe, then Comprehend for text analysis. Flow 3 is the ingest from DynamoDB into Reach Engine.
5) Edge types: triggers and orchestration are 'control'. Writing results and passing payloads are 'data'.
Self-check: 9 visual_connections entries, 10 edges emitted (10 >= 9).

graph.name: Levels Beyond - Media to Cloud Workflow (Reach Engine)
graph.categories: Media & Entertainment, Media Processing, AI/ML Metadata Extraction, Serverless Orchestration
graph.notes: Media to Cloud workflow. A user uploads a media file to S3, which triggers Step Functions. The workflow runs MediaConvert to make a browser-playable proxy, pulls out technical metadata (checksums and frame rates, through Lambdas that are mentioned but not drawn), runs Rekognition video analysis (celebrities, violence, nudity, tied to timecodes), and runs Transcribe and then Comprehend (entities, profanity). All results go into DynamoDB, which is only a temporary store. The data is then ingested into Reach Engine (EC2/EKS) for playback, metadata search and visualization, and for orchestrating delivery to monetization targets outside the platform (possibly hybrid or on the client side).

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Entry point. The user uploads a media file to the S3 bucket, and the upload triggers the Step Functions workflow. It accepts nearly every media format.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates the Media to Cloud workflow. It starts the MediaConvert transcode, triggers Lambdas (mentioned in audio but not drawn) to extract checksums and technical metadata such as frame rates, and then triggers Rekognition and Transcribe.

nodes.name: Elemental MediaConvert
nodes.notes: Transcodes the source into a proxy that plays in the browser, so users can visually check the content alongside the extracted metadata.

nodes.name: Rekognition
nodes.notes: Analyzes the video to detect celebrities, violence, nudity and other content data clients want. Results are tied to timecodes.

nodes.name: Transcribe
nodes.notes: Converts the content's audio into text.

nodes.name: Comprehend
nodes.notes: Analyzes the transcribed text to extract entities and find when profanity occurs.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Temporary data store for all extracted metadata: checksums, technical media info, Rekognition timecoded tags, and Comprehend results. Once the data is stored, it triggers an ingest into Reach Engine.

nodes.name: EC2 (Reach Engine)
nodes.notes: Part of the Reach Engine platform, the core of the product. Supports content playback, viewing and searching metadata, celebrity track visualization, and an orchestration engine that delivers content to monetization targets.

nodes.name: EKS (Reach Engine)
nodes.notes: Part of the Reach Engine platform, hosted together with EC2. Runs the platform's playback, search, visualization and orchestration engine.

edges.notes: The file upload to S3 triggers the Step Functions workflow.
The first step starts the transcode job in MediaConvert to create a browser-playable proxy.
After the proxy is created, technical metadata (checksums, frame rates, media info), extracted through Lambdas according to the audio, is stored in DynamoDB.
After the basic metadata is extracted, another step function triggers Rekognition video analysis.
Timecoded detections (celebrities, violence, nudity) are stored in DynamoDB.
The same step function triggers Transcribe to convert the audio to text.
The transcribed text is sent to Comprehend for analysis.
Text analysis results (entities, profanity occurrences) are stored in DynamoDB.
Once the data is in the temporary DynamoDB store, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered.
Ingest into Reach Engine, which is also hosted on EKS. Added from the audio ('trigger an ingest into Reach Engine'); not a drawn arrow.
